_comment: The one definition of the reviewer feedback on OpenCodeReview findings: the poster renders the legend under every finding from it, and marvin7122/ocr-runners feedback/collect.py and propose.py read reactions and reply keywords with it. Change meanings only here. Keywords with "feedback": false are commands of the apply-replies flow (marvin7122/qlever .opencodereview/apply_replies.py), not feedback on the finding; "scope": "pr" marks those posted as a PR comment instead of a reply. A legacy entry keeps its old meaning for reactions and replies made before the cut-over of `until_version` (the first commit of this file with that version on the default branch).

reactions.meaning: duplicate of the finding on overlapping lines (name it with /duplicate <link>)
confusing → rewritten with a concrete proposal
too long → TL;DR rewrite with a concrete proposal
improvement potential (right idea, the comment should be better)

legacy_reactions.reason: Version 1 of the legend defined 😕 as "not actionable". A 😕 made before the version-2 cut-over keeps that meaning.

keywords.meaning: not actionable as written → rewritten as a concrete, executable proposal
correct, but I won't act on it (no code change; the thread is resolved)
duplicate of the finding at <link> (its URL or #discussion_r<id>); only the original is fixed
move this change into a separate PR, opened and linked here (optional text: its title); removing it from this PR waits for /approve unless the same reply says /approve
how this comment should be better
apply the change proposed in this thread
drop the change proposed in this thread
(as a PR comment, not a reply) act on all reactions and replies: mechanical fixes are committed, the rest is proposed for /approve
(as a PR comment, not a reply) apply every pending proposal

legacy_keywords.reason: Up to version 2, /not-actionable meant "correct, but not worth acting on" (now /skip). A reply made before the version-3 cut-over keeps that meaning.
